issue.title: Update reserved words for MySQL dialect
issue.body:
Update MySQL dialect with reserved words for MariaDB 10.6 (excluding function names in the second symbol list).

Fix: #7167

<!-- Provide a general summary of your proposed changes in the Title field above -->

### Description
This pull request updates the list of reserved words from the MariaDB 10.6 lexer (https://github.com/MariaDB/server/blob/10.6/sql/lex.h) list of symbol names. It does not include the list of function names though.

### Checklist
<!-- go over following points. check them with an `x` if they do apply, (they turn into clickable checkboxes once the PR is submitted, so no need to do everything at once)

-->

This pull request is:

- [X] A short code fix

hey there -

I'm not able to reproduce your failure on mariadb 10.6.4:

```
Welcome to the MariaDB monitor.  Commands end with ; or \g.
Your MariaDB connection id is 11226
Server version: 10.6.4-MariaDB MariaDB Server

Copyright (c) 2000, 2018, Oracle, MariaDB Corporation Ab and others.

Type 'help;' or '\h' for help. Type '\c' to clear the current input statement.

MariaDB [test]> create table leads (id integer, name varchar(20), primary_contact_id integer);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.028 sec)

MariaDB [test]> create table opportunities (id integer, name varchar(20), lead_id integer);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.023 sec)

MariaDB [test]> SELECT DISTINCT opportunities.id, opportunities.name, opportunities.lead_id, lead.id AS "lead__id", lead.name AS "lead__name", lead.primary_contact_id AS "lead__primary_contact_id" FROM opportunities LEFT OUTER JOIN leads AS lead ON opportunities.lead_id = lead.id;
Empty set (0.002 sec)
```

the addition of reserved words seems enormous and beside the above I'm not able to reproduce any problem related to a random sample of words,  "engines", "engine", "fast", and "errors".  I'm able to use these words as table / column names without quoting in mariadb 10.6 and there's no issue:

```
Your MariaDB connection id is 11224
Server version: 10.6.4-MariaDB MariaDB Server

Copyright (c) 2000, 2018, Oracle, MariaDB Corporation Ab and others.

Type 'help;' or '\h' for help. Type '\c' to clear the current input statement.

MariaDB [test]> create table engines (engine varchar(20), errors varchar(30), fast integer);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.025 sec)

MariaDB [test]> show create table engines;
+---------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Table   | Create Table                                                                                                                                                             |
+---------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| engines | CREATE TABLE `engines` (
  `engine` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  `errors` varchar(30) DEFAULT NULL,
  `fast` int(11) DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 |
+---------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.002 sec)

MariaDB [test]> insert into engines (engine, errors, fast) values ('x', 'y', 10);
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.001 sec)

MariaDB [test]> select engine, errors, fast from engines;
+--------+--------+------+
| engine | errors | fast |
+--------+--------+------+
| x      | y      |   10 |
+--------+--------+------+
1 row in set (0.001 sec)

MariaDB [test]> 
```


can you show what your mariadb settings are namely SQL_MODE ?

Indeed many of the words added in the PR seem common enough that they would have caused reports, like `data` or `date`.

There seems to be words more special than others, that require explicit escaping in any case, while other are fine. Is there a way of getting only the explicit escaping ones?
@zzzeek I have since lost access to that particular MariaDB VM, perhaps the owner of the VM @tbilli can check the SQL_MODE for you

Ok at this point, I would need a reproducer to understand the problem.  if there's an odd SQL_MODE setting in play or something, we could detect that instead.   right now i can't reproduce on the same version of the server so i dont want to move on this until we understand the problem.
I have the ansible playbook that setup @tbilli VM.  I will work on reproduction.

https://mariadb.com/kb/en/reserved-words/
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/keywords.html

are the two reserved words list I found (note the MySQL is version dependent) and differs from the lexer in critical ways.

Sorry for the double comment, if it's ok, I'd like to close #7197 and create a new merge request separating the reserved words out of base into it's own file, with links to the reserved words list above it for easier identification in the future. Thoughts?

### Description

1. Move reserved words to it's own file.

> > can you show what your mariadb settings are namely SQL_MODE ?
> 
> Per https://mariadb.com/kb/en/reserved-words/ `leads` and `lead` is not a keyword, `leading` is though.

OK so...what is the bug?   per your original paragraph:

> Which fails with "You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near 'lead ON opportunities.lead_id = lead.id' because lead is not escaped properly as it is not in your set of RESERVED words.

"lead" is not a keyword, so does not need to be escaped?    is the issue perhaps that this is simply a column name that was created with some special case sensitivity or something like that ?  what OS is in use and/or what is the setting for [lower_case_table_names](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/identifier-case-sensitivity.html) ?

I think you mixed up who was commenting @zzzeek 

Updated reserved words list from MariaDB list submitted: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/pull/7207
